user.description: This decides which steps follow and how costs are calculated. You can change it later in the options.

prices.title: Prices
prices.description: All values can be changed later in the options. Efficiency refers to the gross calorific value (Hs), because gas is billed per kWh Hs. For district heating the allocation key matters: only the consumption share is saved when you heat less – the floor-area share is billed regardless. The heat pump therefore has to reach a higher COP to pay off.

boiler.description:

Everything is optional; missing values reduce what the integration can derive.

data.boiler_hwc_mode: Hot water active (ebusd hwcmode, or a binary sensor)
data.boiler_flame: Burner on (binary sensor, e.g. OpenTherm flame, or burner output in %)
data.boiler_flow_setpoint_entity: Without ebusd: flow setpoint of the boiler (number entity)
data.boiler_circulation_l_h: Nominal circulation flow of the pump
data.boiler_nominal_input_kw: Without a gas meter: nominal heat input of the boiler (type plate, kW)
data.boiler_ebus_circuit: ebusd circuit of the boiler (usually bai)
data.boiler_curve_flow_at_minus10: Heating curve: flow temperature at -10 °C outdoor
data.boiler_curve_flow_at_plus15: Heating curve: flow temperature at +15 °C outdoor
data.boiler_hot_water_standby: Keep hot water ready (keep-warm of a combi boiler, cylinder loading)
data.boiler_spread_min_room_share: Share of rooms that must call before the spread judges the curve
data.boiler_load_model: A heating curve of its own per room, for one room, a few rooms and the majority calling
data.boiler_allow_active_control: Release active boiler control (otherwise plan only)

data_description.boiler_nominal_input_kw: Only for the two sensors “Gas for heating” and “Gas for hot water”, and only read when no gas meter is set above. A Vaillant boiler adds up its burner output itself (ebusd PrEnergySumHc1-3 and PrEnergySumHwc1-3); with the nominal heat input from the type plate (Q or Qn, the larger value of a range, e.g. 22.2) that becomes kWh as on the gas bill. Leave empty if you have a gas meter or another boiler.
data_description.boiler_hot_water_standby: Off: with active boiler control, the boiler no longer heats for hot water without a tap open, so it stops firing about once an hour to keep its exchanger warm. A tap still gets hot water, a little later. Leave it on if a hot water cylinder is connected: it would no longer be loaded. Reported by a user, not yet measured on the test installation.
data_description.boiler_spread_min_room_share: The flow/return spread only says something about the heating curve while enough radiators take heat: one open radiator returns the water almost as warm as it went out, and a small spread then used to lower the curve wrongly. With fewer calling rooms than this share of the rooms that can take heat right now (rounded up, at least one), only the progress of the calling rooms counts. Rooms that merely heat along are not counted. 0.5 = half of the rooms. The heating curve per load class counts more rooms than this share as the majority (0.5: three of four rooms).
data_description.boiler_load_model: The flow a flat needs depends on how many radiators take heat, and on each radiator: a small one in a cold room needs a hotter flow than a large one. On: Thriftherm keeps a correction of the heating curve for each room in each of three cases (one room calls, a few, the majority). Of the rooms that want heat, the one that needs the most sets the flow; the others' valves take less. A room that does not get there raises only its own value, so what the bathroom alone taught does not shift the flow for the whole flat. A room without a value starts from its own in the nearest case. A value that has served for some hours counts as found and only moves again on evidence that lasts. Off: one common correction for all rooms and cases, as before; it keeps what it had learned.
data_description.boiler_heat_up_rate_k_h: How fast a room is to warm up while the boiler heats it, for every heat-up of a room that is 1 °C or more below its target (after a raise, the setback or an open window). Slower than this, Thriftherm raises the flow for this room every 20 minutes and remembers per room how much it took, as the start for its next heat-up; much faster, it lowers it again. More speed burns more gas. Only acts with active boiler control. 0 leaves the flow as before: heating curve, learned correction and up to 8 °C extra while a room is far below target.
data_description.boiler_flame: Only needed without a gas meter and without status codes (ebusd), e.g. with OpenTherm. Thriftherm takes the best burner sign there is: the gas flow first, then the boiler's status code, then this sensor, else the pump.
data_description.gas_flow: Also tells Thriftherm when the burner runs. Enter it only if it shows the flame within about a minute; a slow pulse sensor is better left empty, then the boiler's status code counts. The meter reading (volume) is enough for gas by purpose.

midea.title: Heat pump (optional add-on)
midea.description: Optional. Leave everything empty to use the smart boiler control only; the heat pump can be added later in the options. Intake/outlet sensors and the airflow curve are needed for the COP. Airflow curve format: rpm:m3h,rpm:m3h (e.g. 400:250,900:600).

data.midea_duct_factor: Duct factor (real airflow / free-blowing, 1.0 without hoses)
data.heat_pump_cop_profile: COP values of this model (without sensors at the unit)
data.midea_follow_rooms: Setpoint follows the served rooms' target (plus the setpoint offset from “Heat pump: fine tuning”); the unit regulates by itself
data.midea_room: Room the heat pump stands in

data_description.heat_pump_cop_profile: Without a smart plug and sensors at the intake and outlet, Thriftherm cannot measure the COP and decides on a general starting curve. Pick your model to decide on values measured on the same model instead. What your own unit measures always comes first.

parameters.title: Control parameters
parameters.description: The values of everyday use come first. The sections below them rarely need a change.

data.override_default_min: How long a change by hand is respected (thermostat and heat pump)

data.room_allow_active_control: Release active room control (write setpoints to the thermostats)

data_description.room_echo_filter: Better Thermostat rewrites the valve setpoint every few seconds. Over Zigbee a reply can arrive after the next write, and Better Thermostat then takes the old value for a turn of the knob. Thriftherm used to turn that into a two-hour override. With the filter on, a jump back to a value the valve already showed and left within the last minute (e.g. 16 → 16.5 → 16) is ignored and the plan's setpoint is sent again. A real turn of the knob on the thermostat or a change in the app brings a new value and is still taken over. Only applies to rooms whose thermostat is a Better Thermostat. Recommended: on.

reset_learning.title: Reset learning
reset_learning.description: After a change to the installation, learned values no longer fit – for example after hydraulic balancing, new radiators, fitted ducts or a new thermostat. Only the chosen areas are cleared; settings, schedules and modes stay. When the heating curve, duct factor, installation room, served rooms or a room's sensor change, Thriftherm forgets the affected area on its own.

set_override.name: Set room override
set_override.description: Temporarily override a room's target temperature. Expires automatically.

clear_override.name: Back to automatic
clear_override.description: End what was changed by hand. With a room: that room's override. Without: every override and quick heat-up, and the heat pump's time in hand after a change at the unit.

set_away.name: Set away
set_away.description: Switch to away mode, optionally with a return time for preheating.

return_time.name: Return time
return_time.description: Expected return. Omit to keep a return time that is already set.

clear_return_time.name: Open-ended
clear_return_time.description: Drop a return time set earlier, so the absence has no planned end.

reset_learning.name: Reset learning data
reset_learning.description: Forgets what was learned in the chosen areas. Settings and run state stay.

scope.name: Areas
scope.description: boiler, heat_pump and/or rooms. All when omitted.

rooms.name: Rooms
rooms.description: Room keys; narrows the rooms area. All rooms when omitted.

boost.name: Quick heat-up
boost.description: Heat a room to its comfort temperature as fast as possible (heat pump at full power).

no_schedule.title: {room}: no heating window configured
no_schedule.description: {room} has neither a schedule helper nor a time range. The room stays at its setback temperature for good and is never pre-heated. Create a schedule under Settings → Devices & services → Helpers and select it for the room in the options.

airflow_not_calibrated.title: Heat pump airflow not calibrated
airflow_not_calibrated.description: Without the rpm → m³/h curve there is no thermal power and therefore no COP. The cost comparison falls back to the data sheet until then. The curve lives in the heat pump options.

boiler_data_unavailable.title: No data from the boiler
boiler_data_unavailable.description: ebusd is not delivering usable values right now. Nothing is sent to the boiler; it keeps running on its own front knob. Check the ebusd app and the eBUS adapter.

schedule_missing.title: {room}: schedule helper missing
schedule_missing.description: {room} refers to the schedule {entity_id}, which no longer exists in Home Assistant. The room has no warm periods left and stays at its setback temperature. Recreate the helper or pick another one in the options.

heat_stays_in_the_room.title: Heat pump assigned to rooms it cannot reach
heat_stays_in_the_room.description: The heat pump is set to serve {rooms}, but no duct factor is configured (1.0 means no ducts fitted), so the warm air stays in the room the unit stands in. Until that changes, a run for those rooms heats the wrong one. Either fit the ducts and set the factor in the options, or clear the tick for those rooms.

thermostat_silent.title: {room}: radiator thermostat not responding
thermostat_silent.description: The radiator thermostat in {room} has not reported for over two and a half hours. It keeps its last setpoint and takes no new ones, so the room no longer calls the boiler. Check the thermostat: take the batteries out and put them back in, or look for it in Zigbee2MQTT.

not_loaded.message: Thriftherm is not set up or not loaded.

return_time_in_past.message: The return time must be in the future.

setback_above_comfort.message: {room}: the setback temperature must not be above the comfort temperature.
